extracted.intended_audience: general public / viewers of Last Week Tonight interested in net neutrality advocacy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and calls-to-action for members of the public to submit comments to the FCC opposing rollback of net neutrality, including recommended message content and a suggested technical shortcut (gofccyourself.com).

rubrics_metrics.name: Message content — support Title II oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell Ajit Pai and the FCC that 'you support strong net neutrality backed by Title II oversight of ISP’s.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oliver emphasized that the 'last part' (Title II oversight of ISPs) is really important; the article reproduces the exact phrasings viewers were asked to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gofccyourself.com to simplify submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the FCC comment process seems 'too complicated,' use the URL 'gofccyourself.com' which John Oliver said will take care of Steps 1-5 of the FCC comment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site is presented as a technical shortcut to avoid having to manually perform the multi-step submission; recommended for viewers who find the official process cumbersome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect and plan for a multi-step FCC comment process
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC has made it much harder to comment this time, requiring 'six complicated steps' to leave a remark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for multiple procedural steps (the article does not enumerate them) and consider using tools or guides to complete them; gofccyourself.com reportedly handles most of these steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment — 5 to 10 minutes of effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Oliver asked viewers to spend 'just 5 to 10 minutes of minor effort' to submit a comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames this as a small time investment compared with other trivial online activities many people find time for, so plan to set aside that short window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument content — explain harm of ending net neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: Include explanation that ending net neutrality would 'choke[s] their choices on the web' and otherwise describe the harms of rollback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference accessible explanations (as Oliver did in 2014) about how ending net neutrality would limit consumer choice and favor ISPs; persuasive, concrete examples of harm may strengthen the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobilization tactic — rally internet communities to flood comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Call on 'the Internet time-wasters and troublemakers' (Oliver's phrasing) and other audiences to 'mob the comments section' and 'turn on their caps lock' to overwhelm the FCC comment system with pro-net-neutrality submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames this as a repeat of a previous successful tactic (2014) that crashed the FCC comments system; it implies coordinated mass commenting as an effective advocacy strategy.
